pitch fader as a fraction; 0.08 is +8%
how far the pitch fader reaches either side, in percent; does not move the tempo
make this deck a double of another: same record, place, speed and key, in step
pitch fader by its own travel, -1 to +1, across the deck's pitch range
hold the musical key while the pitch fader changes tempo
let the pitch fader move tempo and key together
flip keylock
keep a shadow playhead running while a loop or a censor diverts this one
stop shadowing, and stay where the playhead is
flip slip mode
play backwards
play forwards again
flip the direction of travel
hold the censor: reverse over a word, and land back on the beat
release the censor
cut the motor and coast to a stop over this many beats, like a turntable losing power
put the motor back on, wherever the record got to
throw the record backwards and let friction take it down over this many beats
put the motor back on after a backspin
hold one of the eight slices of the current span; releases with `slice_off`, and the track lands where it would have been
let a held slice go
how many beats the eight slices divide up; 4, 8, 16 or 32 in practice
toggle one stem: vocal, drums, bass or other
hold only one stem in the deck mix
release a held stem solo
set one stem level as stem:value, with value from 0 to 1
hold a loop roll this many beats long, as a decimal or 1/4 — the track carries on underneath
release the roll, and land where the track would have been
change an effect slot: `fx <1-3> <none|echo|delay|reverb|gate|crush|flanger|phaser|filter>` to load one, then `on`/`off`/`toggle`, `wet <0-1>`, `beats <0.0625-4>`, `amount <0-1>`, `pre`/`post`
transpose in semitones for harmonic mixing, without changing tempo
match tempo and phase to the other playing deck; refused if either grid is weak
release the tempo lock and give the pitch fader back
move the playhead by whole beats; negative goes back
jump to a hot cue, or set it here if the slot is empty
set a hot cue at the playhead, replacing whatever was there
forget a hot cue
loop this many beats from here, as a decimal or 1/4; 0 turns looping off
stop looping and carry on
halve the loop, keeping its start
double the loop, keeping its start
drop the loop's in point at the playhead
drop the out point and start looping
slide the whole loop by whole beats, keeping its length
channel fader
trim, in decibels
low band; 0 is a true kill, 1 is flat
mid band; 0 is a true kill, 1 is flat
high band; 0 is a true kill, 1 is flat
filter sweep; -1 fully low-passed, 0 off, +1 fully high-passed
how much of the recorded singer to leave in, for karaoke: 1 as recorded, 0.25 a guide vocal, 0 out
send this deck to the headphones
stop sending this deck to the headphones
flip the headphone cue send
put this deck on the left half of the crossfader
put this deck on the right half of the crossfader
take this deck off the crossfader; it plays whatever the crossfader does
put a beat on the playhead, leaving the tempo alone
slide the whole beat grid by milliseconds; negative is earlier
multiply the grid tempo, keeping the anchor; 2 and 0.5 fix an octave error
set the grid tempo outright, keeping the anchor
tap along with the music; two taps give a tempo and the last sets the phase
throw away grid edits and go back to what the analyser found
keep the loop that is playing in a numbered slot, with the track
put a saved loop back and start looping it
crossfader; -1 is the decks assigned left, +1 the decks assigned right
constant-power crossfader, for long blends (the default)
linear crossfader, for the same record on both decks
sharp-cut crossfader, for scratching: full volume a few millimetres in

the sampler: `sampler <1-8> trigger|release|stop|clear`, `sampler <1-8> one_shot|hold|loop|stutter` to set how a pad behaves, `sampler <1-8> volume <0-1>`, `master`/`cue` to route it, `sync`/`sync_off`; and `sampler bank <1-4>`, `sampler volume <0-1>`, `sampler stop_all`

record into a slot of the bank showing: `sampler record <1-8> master` takes what the room hears, `sampler record <1-8> deck <n>` takes that deck before its fader; then `sampler record stop` to keep it or `sampler record cancel` to bin it
change a master effect slot; the same grammar as a deck's, applied to the whole mix
master output level in decibels
booth monitor level in decibels
the music's level in the singers' monitor in decibels, apart from the room's; the bottom is off
a monitor of their own for each singer, where the output has a pair for each
the singers share one monitor again
headphone blend; 0 is all cue, 1 is all master
cue in one ear, master in the other
return the headphones to a blend
record the master to disk; the file lands beside the settings, named for when it started
stop recording and finish the file
snap beat jumps to the grid
let beat jumps move by an exact beat from wherever you are
put the next singer's song on that deck, in their key, with the voice they asked for
mix the next singer's song in from what the room hears, at the next phrase
the singer up next has sung: they go to the back of the rotation
emergency: take every control back, clear every effect, flatten the tone
engage the master limiter (on by default)
bypass the master limiter, for an external processor downstream

builtin:autopilot.name: Autopilot
builtin:autopilot.about: Driving and being driven, on Space a: a a lets the automix mix, a o takes it back, a n mixes now; a p the autopilot's panel, a r how the room is taking it.

keys.label: Mix to the next record now

builtin:dashboards.name: Dashboards
builtin:dashboards.about: Working from the boards, on Space g: g and a board's own key from Space b goes there, g 0 is the launcher, g g the decks again, and Shift and a panel's key from Space o opens that panel large.

builtin:essentials.name: Essentials
builtin:essentials.about: The handful every mix uses, on Space e, for the current deck: e p plays, e c cues, e s syncs, e l loops four beats; e 1 and e 2 load what is chosen in the library.

keys.label: Load the chosen record on deck 1
Load the chosen record on deck 2

builtin:karaoke-host.name: Karaoke host
builtin:karaoke-host.about: The rotation, the microphone and the singer's key on Space k: k 1 or k 2 puts the next singer on a deck, k b brings them in, k s says they have sung; k u, k d and k h move the current deck's key.

keys.label: The current deck a semitone up
The current deck a semitone down
The current deck home, in its own key
The current deck's vocal out or back

builtin:learning.name: Learning
builtin:learning.about: The teacher on Space l: l c the course, l p the practice lab, l r a mix rehearsed between two records, l g the guide to learning, l k every key.

keys.label: The guide to a first mix

builtin:one-hand.name: One hand
builtin:one-hand.about: Everything a night needs from one hand on Space h, for a DJ holding a microphone or working a laptop on its own: play, the crossfader, sync, the next mix.

keys.label: Mix to the next record now

builtin:open-format.name: Open format
builtin:open-format.about: For nights that jump between tempos and styles, on Space f: a wide pitch range for records far apart, a double of the record playing, sync and the automix.

keys.label: Mix to the next record now

builtin:performance.name: Performance
builtin:performance.about: The current deck played hard, on Space x: x 1 to x 8 are its hot cues; x l a loop (x l 1 to x l 8 beats, x l h halves, x l d doubles, x l o off); x j jumps (x j 1, x j 4, x j 8 forward, x J back); slip, reverse and brake on x s, x r and x b.

builtin:scratch.name: Scratch
builtin:scratch.about: The crossfader's curve and the decks' sides on Space c: c s for a sharp cut, c b back to a blend, c 1 and c 2 to put the decks on their sides.
